title: Diabetes (Madhumeha): Causes, Diet and Daily Routine from the Ayurvedic View
excerpt: More than 10 crore people in India live with diabetes. Learn how Ayurveda understands Madhumeha (Prameha) — causes, symptoms, tests, what to eat and avoid, daily routine, yoga and important precautions.
content:
Diabetes (Madhumeha) is rising fast in India. According to the ICMR-INDIAB study (2023), more than 10 crore people in India have diabetes and about 13.6 crore have pre-diabetes — they are on the verge of high blood sugar. Many of them do not even know that their sugar is high.

The good news is that with the right diet, a regular daily routine and timely tests, diabetes can be kept well under control, and many people with pre-diabetes can stop it from progressing. Ayurveda places the greatest emphasis on exactly this way of living.

What is diabetes?

Our body uses a hormone called insulin to turn the sugar (glucose) from food into energy. When the body cannot make enough insulin, or the insulin it makes does not work properly, sugar stays high in the blood — this is called diabetes.

  • Type 1: The body makes almost no insulin. It usually begins in childhood or youth. Insulin is essential here — it must never be stopped.
  • Type 2: The most common type. Wrong eating habits, little physical work, belly fat, stress and family history are its main causes.
  • Diabetes in pregnancy (gestational): Sugar rises during pregnancy. A doctor's care is essential for both mother and baby.

Diabetes in Ayurveda — “Prameha”

Ayurveda calls such urinary disorders Prameha and describes 20 types — 10 Kaphaja, 6 Pittaja and 4 Vataja. Madhumeha is one Vataja type, in which the urine becomes sweet like madhu (honey).

According to Ayurveda, Prameha usually begins with an increase of Kapha dosha and Meda (fat) and a weak Agni (digestive fire). As the disease becomes chronic, Vata rises and the body's dhatus (tissues) start to waste — then weakness, weight loss and nerve problems appear. That is why Ayurvedic treatment is not limited to lowering sugar; it aims to balance Agni, the doshas and the dhatus.

आस्यासुखं स्वप्नसुखं दधीनि ग्राम्यौदकानूपरसाः पयांसि।
नवान्नपानं गुडवैकृतं च प्रमेहहेतुः कफकृच्च सर्वम्॥

Meaning: The comfort of sitting all the time, excessive sleep, curd, heavy meat soups, too much milk, new grain, things made from jaggery — and everything that increases Kapha — are causes of Prameha. (Charaka Samhita, Chikitsa Sthana 6)

Main causes

  • Sitting all day, no physical work or exercise
  • Sleeping during the day and staying up late at night
  • Frequent sweets, maida (refined flour), cold drinks, packaged juices and fried food
  • Eating without hunger, overeating, heavy meals late at night
  • Extra fat around the belly and waist
  • Constant stress, worry and poor sleep
  • Diabetes in parents, brothers or sisters

Symptoms — do not ignore them

  • Frequent urination, especially at night
  • Excessive thirst, dry mouth
  • Constant tiredness and weakness
  • Wounds or injuries healing slowly
  • Blurred vision
  • Tingling, burning or numbness in hands and feet
  • Repeated skin, urine or gum infections
  • Weight loss without reason

Remember — type 2 diabetes often has no symptoms in the beginning. So after the age of 30–35, and even earlier if diabetes runs in the family or weight is high, get your sugar tested at least once a year.

Tests — what sugar level is normal?

  • Fasting sugar: below 100 mg/dL normal • 100–125 pre-diabetes • 126 or more diabetes
  • HbA1c (average of the last 3 months): below 5.7% normal • 5.7–6.4% pre-diabetes • 6.5% or more diabetes
  • 2 hours after a meal (PP): below 140 mg/dL normal • 140–199 pre-diabetes • 200 or more diabetes

Diabetes is not diagnosed from a single report; the doctor confirms it by repeating the test. People with diabetes should check regularly at home with a glucometer and get HbA1c done every 3 months.

Diet — what to eat

For Prameha, Ayurveda recommends food that is light, dry, Kapha-reducing and bitter or astringent in taste.

  • Barley (Yava): considered the best grain for a Prameha patient in Ayurveda. Barley roti, porridge or sattu.
  • Millets: bajra, jowar, ragi, kangni (foxtail millet) — can also be mixed into wheat flour.
  • Old grain: according to Ayurveda, grain stored for a year is lighter than new grain.
  • Pulses: moong, chana, arhar (toor), kulthi (horse gram).
  • Vegetables: bitter gourd (karela), fenugreek leaves (methi), bottle gourd, ridge gourd, pointed gourd (parwal), tinda, pumpkin, spinach, bathua and other greens.
  • Fruits (in limited quantity): jamun (in season), amla, guava, papaya, apple.
  • Kitchen spices: turmeric, fenugreek seeds, cinnamon, cumin, ajwain.
  • Water: lukewarm water, or water boiled and cooled.

How to plan your plate

Keep half the plate vegetables, one quarter dal/protein and one quarter grain (barley, bajra, a little rice or roti). Eat salad and vegetables first, grains later. Eat slowly, chew well and stop a little before you are full.

What to avoid or greatly reduce

  • Sugar, sweets, jaggery — jaggery and honey also raise sugar; being “natural” does not make them safe
  • Maida, white bread, biscuits, namkeen, fast food
  • Cold drinks, packaged juices, sweetened tea and coffee
  • Fried food, too much ghee and oil
  • Too much rice, potato, sweet potato and sweet fruits (mango, chikoo, grapes, banana) in large amounts
  • Curd — especially at night; thin buttermilk (chaach) can be taken instead
  • Snacking again and again, and eating late at night

Daily routine and exercise

In Prameha, Ayurveda considers physical work and exercise as important as medicine.

  • Wake up before sunrise
  • Walk briskly for 30–45 minutes every day; a slow 10–15 minute walk after each meal also helps
  • Do not sleep during the day
  • Keep dinner light and eat it 2–3 hours before bedtime
  • Sleep 7–8 hours every night
  • Practise meditation, japa or prayer to reduce stress
  • Stay completely away from smoking and alcohol

Yoga and pranayama

  • Asanas: Surya Namaskar, Mandukasana, Vajrasana (after meals), Paschimottanasana, Ardha Matsyendrasana, Bhujangasana, Dhanurasana
  • Pranayama: Anulom-Vilom, Kapalbhati, Bhramari

Learn yoga only from a trained teacher. If you have heart disease, high BP, eye problems, hernia or a recent operation, ask your Vaidya/doctor before doing Kapalbhati or difficult asanas.

Ayurvedic herbs — with caution

Ayurvedic texts and several modern studies mention some herbs for Prameha, such as Gudmar (Madhunashini), Vijaysar, jamun seed, fenugreek, Giloy (Guduchi), turmeric and amla (the Nisha-Amalaki combination). But:

  • Which medicine, in what dose and for how long — this is decided only after looking at each person's prakriti, nadi (pulse), age, sugar reports and current medicines.
  • Taking herbs on your own along with allopathic medicines or insulin can make sugar fall too low. So whenever you start any new medicine, check your sugar more often.
  • Never stop or reduce your current medicine or insulin on your own. When sugar is under control, change medicines only on the doctor's advice.
  • Beware of products that claim to “cure diabetes 100% from the root”.

If sugar falls too low (hypoglycaemia)

In people taking medicines or insulin, sugar sometimes falls very low (below 70 mg/dL). Symptoms: sudden sweating, shaking, anxiety, dizziness, strong hunger, fast heartbeat or confusion.

  • Immediately drink 3–4 teaspoons of sugar or glucose dissolved in water, or half a glass of fruit juice.
  • Check sugar again after 15 minutes; if it is still low, take it again.
  • If the patient is unconscious or cannot swallow, do not put anything in the mouth — take them to hospital immediately.

When to see a doctor immediately

  • Sugar repeatedly very high (for example above 300 mg/dL)
  • Vomiting, severe weakness, fast breathing, stomach pain or drowsiness/unconsciousness
  • A foot wound that is not healing, swelling, pus or skin turning black
  • Sudden loss of vision or chest pain

Foot care

In diabetes the nerves and blood circulation of the feet can weaken, so even a small injury can become a big wound. Look at your feet carefully every day, do not walk barefoot, wear comfortable shoes, cut nails carefully and apply oil on cracked heels.

Summary — points to remember

  • Test sugar at least once a year — even without symptoms
  • Barley, millets, pulses and green vegetables; stop sweets, maida and cold drinks
  • Daily walking, yoga, meals on time and full sleep
  • Do not stop medicines on your own; keep getting regular tests
  • Ayurvedic treatment only on the advice of an experienced Vaidya

Sources: Charaka Samhita, Chikitsa Sthana 6 (Prameha Chikitsa); ICMR-INDIAB study, The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology (2023); diagnostic criteria of the American Diabetes Association.
